note: tools/radar-redraw.py's spec. Scope numbers are in the original's file pixels (rows top down); everything under marks is in the game's view (rows flipped, as the cockpit shows the frames). Geometry is measured from the player's own export each run; these are only the search windows and the drawing choices.

scope.line_note: graticule lines 0.7 original px wide; line_edge null: a one-texel anti-aliased edge (crisp; round 2-3 used a 0.25 px ramp)

stamps.note: the sprites the game stamps over every frame (the cockpit layout's zrad.map block): sheets, their sprites' rows (rows as shown), the anchor and size (original px, game view). The redrawn sheets carry the frame's texels inside mask_radius of the frame's own corner scope / lamp and are keyed outside; lit faces from profiles measured on the original sprites

A.note: faithful: the original's line and cone, its colours, no afterglow barbs

B.note: phosphor: a thin sharp beam with a bright core and an afterglow fading behind it (the side the beam has left), a soft-edged cone; the graticule printed crisp over all of them (grid_over)

marks.ink_note: ink_multiply: the printed marks and words darken the panel's own shade to this fraction (printed, its shading showing through); without it they are laid in the flat ink colour

B612.name: B612
B612.by: The B612 Project Authors (Airbus, Intactile Design, Nicolas Chauveau, Thomas Paillot, Jonathan Favre-Lamarine, Jean-Luc Vinot)

label_sets.name: lock-range
label_sets.note: the owner's lead: the top knob is the lock tone's volume (LOCK VOL), the lower the range: 100, TGT and 600 lettered in place of the painted left tick, X and right tick (the pointer rests on 600: the default), RANGE on the one-pixel row; every word one cap height (2.4 px; LOCK VOL was 2.6, the others 1.8-1.9). 100 m and 600 m are the game's two radar ranges (R); TGT is a design story, not a state of R (the radar camera is its own toggle, W); 100, TGT and 600 lifted 0.4 px out from the knob, along the line from its centre

texts.note: centred on the left tick the word replaces
on the right tick, lifted 0.4 px out from the knob like the others and 0.8 px left: the scope bezel's outer edge is at x 41.0 on these rows, the ink must end a pixel short of it (a test checks)
on the one-pixel row (y 90), centred under the knob (x 30) rather than on the row's own ink (x 27-39)

label_sets.name: lock-range-m
label_sets.note: as lock-range with the unit: 100m / TGT / 600m (the game's real ranges)

texts.note: pulled in from the tick line: further out it would run into the scope bezel (x 43 at this height)
on the one-pixel row (y 90), centred under the knob (x 30) rather than on the row's own ink (x 27-39)

label_sets.name: owner-50-500
label_sets.note: the owner's literal words: 50m / TGT / 500m, RANGE under; NOT the game's ranges (100 m and 600 m)

texts.note: pulled in from the tick line: further out it would run into the scope bezel (x 43 at this height)
on the one-pixel row (y 90), centred under the knob (x 30) rather than on the row's own ink (x 27-39)

label_sets.name: var-range
label_sets.note: fit rank 1: VAR RANGE is the best-scoring radar label between the knobs in both row orders (z 1.7, inside chance); the two-position knob = power (OFF ON z 1.6 in the 1-pixel row)

label_sets.name: gain-range
label_sets.note: fit rank 2 (VIDEO GAIN z 0.8 game view, 2.0 file view); strongest context: the two-position knob = the game's two ranges, 100 m and 600 m

label_sets.name: intensity
label_sets.note: fit rank 3 (INTENSITY z 0.0 / 1.0; LO HI z 2.3 in the 1-pixel row): the reference consoles' word for a stepped knob

label_sets.name: marks-only
label_sets.note: no words: the original's blobs kept where they are, cleaned

edges.note: the unit's wires and the bezel rings drawn again from the original's own colours about fitted curves (radar-redraw.py, the edges). Game view. zone: where the wires lie, left of the body's left edge (x 7) or below its bottom edge (y 102), in box, clear of the scope's bezel by clear_of_scope px; the original's transparent pixels there are cleared (the upscale's smeared alpha gone), the wires drawn over

corners.note: the body's bottom left corner: a circle fitted to the silhouette's pixel edges in box, its bevel drawn again over the quarter arc (degrees, game view, 90 = down, 180 = left), the straight sides past it left as they are. mode silhouette: only the outline is made round (alpha), the upscale's shading kept (the regressed bevel did not meet the upscale's straight sides)
the body's bottom right corner, likewise

wires.name: cable
wires.note: the dark grey cable round the left side and under the body: one tube, its width its pixels over its length, its shading regressed along it

wires.name: pair
wires.note: the red and orange twisted pair: one tube; which colour each texel is follows the original's pixels (smoothed), each colour shaded as the original shades it

rings.note: the scope's bezel: from just inside the face's edge out to d (over the panel) or d_free (where the original is transparent beyond: the silhouette at the bottom). skip (degrees, game view, 0 = right, -90 = up): the top, where the original's ring runs into the body's top edge; under_inset: left out within the corner scope's face radius plus this, where its ring lies over the bezel
